== Biography ==
Moses and Sarah had 11 children.

'''Obituary'''

Anderson - Mrs. Sarah Anderson was born near Bakerstown, Allegheny co., Pa., May 9 1808, of pious Covenanter parents, and was reared in the faith of that church.  Her maiden name was Glasgow, being a daughter of Mr. John Glasgow, long a ruling elder in the Pine Creek Covenanter congregation. After her marriage to Mr. Moses T. Anderson, she joined with him in the membership of the United Presbyterian Church, and was long a member of the Freeport congregation.

Mrs. Anderson reared a large family, many of whom became eminent in the learned professions and officers in the Church of Christ.

She came near to filling the scriptural ideal of womanhood, possessing a most sweet and amiable disposition.  She was at once pious, unselfish, peaceful, and charitable.  She was so trustful in the wisdom and righteousness of God, that she was perfectly satisfied with any ordering of his providence.  Her Christian deportment in every relation of life soon won for her the affection and respect of a large circle of acquaintances.

Without much physical suffering, and with perfect trust in her Saviour, she passed into the realms of the eternal world on Jan. 31 1894, in the 86th year of her age.  Triumphing over all the difficulties of life and death, she leaves a bright example to be followed and a memory to be blessed.  Her remains were interred in the Freeport cemetery amidst the dust of her kindred, awaiting the resurrection morn.  "She is not dead, but sleepeth." W.M.G.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-209]] is assessed at 97% (proved). Sarah’s obituary after her 31 January 1894 death explicitly calls her a daughter of John Glasgow, long a ruling elder of Pine Creek Covenanter congregation. That distinctive church role and her 9 May 1808 Bakerstown birth select this John convincingly.

Selected father-profile identity and paternal relationship; maternal identity is separate.
